result.text: If an insurant could be possibly subrogated against, I get information about that.
I check that case and if the possibility is really there, I send a request for payment to the insurant and make me a reminder.
If recourse is not possible, I close the case.
When we receive the money, I make a booking and close the case.
If the insurant disagrees with the recourse, I'll have to check the reasoning of that.
If he is right, I simply close the case.
If he is wrong, I forward the case to a collection agency.
It the deadline for disagreement is reached and we haven't received any money, I forward the case to the collection agency as well.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.

result.rule: When the description states that an activity or decision outcome leads to another activity or a terminal outcome, including on a conditional branch: Model sequence flows connecting the stated nodes in the described order, preserving each described branch through its next activity or terminal outcome.

When the description states that a later activity occurs only after an earlier activity succeeds: Model the success outcome as a decision and connect its success path to the dependent activity in the stated order; preserve any other stated outcome paths.

When the description states distinct decisions or approvals at different points in the process: Model each decision or approval at the point stated, and connect it to the activities that precede and follow it in the described order; do not replace one decision with another.

When the description presents activities or events in a chronological sequence, including how the process begins: Connect the corresponding BPMN elements with sequence flows in the stated order, including a flow from the start event to the first activity and flows between successive activities.

trace.reason: Check existing collaboration and pool guidelines before proposing a rule about the absent reference pool.

result.rule: Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers modeling the first-person narrator as a participant.

result.rule: When the description states that a participant performs a distinct activity after a condition is met: Model the activity as a BPMN task and connect it to the surrounding process flow.

When the description mentions an external person or organization as the recipient of a request, the source of a response or payment, or the destination of a referral, but does not describe that party’s own process or responsibilities: model the stated work and events within the modeled participant; do not create separate participant pools or message flows solely because of that mention

When the description states that a participant performs a distinct action to initiate the process: Model a start event for the process trigger, followed by a task for the initiating action; do not use the start event to represent the action itself.

When the description presents activities or events in a chronological sequence, including how the process begins: Connect the corresponding BPMN elements with sequence flows in the stated order, including a flow from the start event to the first activity and flows between successive activities.
